51527680.DESCRIPTION: Inhibition of 6His tagged NOXO1 (149 to 286 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) assessed as apparent dissociation constant at 800 uM by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 2.6.1. Isotherma: A MicroCal VP-ITC calorimeter (MicroCal Inc., Northampton, USA) was used to quantify the complex formation between Noxo1 (p47phox), Cyba (p22phox), and Nox inhibitors. The NOXO1 protein, comprising 138 amino acids and purified from E. coli, and the 25-amino acid CYBA peptide (Ala, Ala, Glu, Gly, Gly, Lys, Lys, Leu, Asn, Pro, Pro, Pro, Pro, Pro, Pro, Gln, Arg, Arg, Ser, Ser, Ser) chemically synthesized, were used in the study. Dialysis was performed on all samples using ITC buffer at 18 °C (50 mM HEPES and 150 mM sodium chloride, 1 mM dithiothreitol, pH 7.4). Cyba peptide was dissolved in ITC buffer. In the first titration, a solution of 40 μM protein in the cell was titrated by injection of a total of 250 μL of 800 μM peptide in the syringe in 25 total injections. In the second titration, a solution of 40 μM inhibitor 1 in the cell was titrated by injection of a total of 250 μL of 800 μM protein in the syringe in 25 aliquots. In the third titration, a solution of 40 μM protein in the cell was titrated by injection of a total of 250 μL of 800 μM inhibitor 2 in the syringe in 25 aliquots. In the fourth titration, the complex of 40 μM protein and 200 μM of inhibitor 2 in the cell were titrated by injection of a total 250 μL of 800 μM peptide in the syringe in 25 injections. In the fifth titration complex of 40 μM protein and 200 μM of inhibitor 3 in the cell were titrated by injection of a total 250 μL of 800 μM peptide in the syringe in 25 injections. In the sixth titration complex of 40 μM protein and 200 μM of inhibitor 4 in the cell were titrated by injection of a total of 250 μL of 800 μM peptide in the syringe in 25 injections. Origin version 7.0 software was used to calculate temperatures of dilution. By titrating the Cyba peptide into ITC buffer and subtracting it from the raw ITC data. The single-site and double-site binding models were used to analyze the dissociation constant.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - 3.3. Biophysica: In this study we used isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) to quantify the interaction between Noxo1 protein and Cyba peptide in presence and absence of the synthesized inhibitors. Isothermal titration calorimetry measures heat released during binding. In this method, the ligand interacts with a protein under a constant temperature. First, ITC was performed by examining the interaction between Noxo1 SH3 domains and the Cyba peptide. A mixture of the Noxo1 protein (40 μM) was placed in the sample cell and the Cyba peptide (800 μM) was titrated by syringe at 18 °C. Data was analyzed using Origin software. The result showed that the Cyba peptide bound to SH3 domains of Noxo1 protein with an apparent kD 1.1 ± 0.4 μM using a single site binding model, Figure 4A and Table 1. The binding affinity corresponds to known literature values reference. To examine the binding interaction between Noxo1 and Cyba peptide in the presence of inhibitor 1, we titrated Cyba peptide into a pre-formed complex of Noxo1 and inhibitor 1, as shown in Figure 4B and Table 1. However, under similar conditions, only a modest change in binding interaction between Noxo1 and Cyba peptide in the presence of inhibitor 1 was observed (kD 4.1 ± 0.2 μM). We then examined inhibitor 2 under the same conditions. Figure 4C shows that the data best fit a two binding sites model. Both binding sites were exothermic and had enthalpy changes of 7.7 ± 0.35 Kcal/mole and 5.2 ± 0.30Kcal/mole. The apparent Kd was 0.002 ± 0.001 μM and 3.7 ± 6 μM respectively. Next, to examine the binding interaction between Noxo1 and Cyba peptide in the presence of inhibitor 2, we titrated a Cyba peptide into a pre-formed complex of Noxo1 and inhibitor 2 in Figure 4D and Table 1. The observed Kd to the mixture was 39 ± 8 μM, a reduction of 39-fold. Two more compounds were synthesized to identify the importance of the PEG and piperidine rings combinations on binding. Inhibitor 3 is formed by adding methyl-terminated two polyethyleneglycol chain to inhibitor 1 and therefore lacks the terminal biotin. Inhibitor 4 lacks the biphenyl ring and instead has an N-Benzyl methyl amine. Findings demonstrated that inhibitor 3 showed an apparent Kd of 44 ± 1 μM when NOXO1 and CYBA peptide were examined, see Figure 4E. This indicates the polyethyleneglycol and the biphenyl ring are needed for inhibition. In contrast, inhibitor 4 could not compete with the Noxo1-Cyba interaction as shown in Figure 4F. The apparent Kd was 2.3 ± 1 μM or similar binding to the solution lacking any inhibitor. Thus inhibitor 4 shows that the biphenyl ring is needed for inhibition. These data show that despite the increased docking score induced by the addition of biotin, it is not necessary for binding.
